rationale: This is the archive's best performer (Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield) with `xrd` subtracted from the numerator — a cosmetic merge with the already-tested R&D-hurdle family that changes nothing for the majority of firms where `xrd` is missing/zero, so it cannot cleanly attribute any incremental effect.

The primary leg is book-equity growth scaled by market value, whose positive expected sign contradicts the well-documented investment/asset-growth anomaly (and will be partly absorbed by CMA in the FF5 alpha), while the `ABS(DELTA(ceq)-ib)` penalty conflates issuance and repurchase — two effects with opposite known return signs.

The interaction is coherent and explicitly diagnoses the earlier After-Interest Claim Yield failure (strong slope, no alpha) as leverage-driven cheapness, though the conditioning leg is essentially the known debt-issuance anomaly, so any success may be attributable to that rather than to the interaction.

It retains the archive's strongest structure but adds a genuinely new, evidence-motivated dimension (capital-consumption burden) to explain why depreciation-based value legs produced negative alphas; the risk is that `dp/at` largely proxies industry capital intensity rather than value-trap risk.

The valuation leg collapses to a near-standard earnings yield (dividends are small relative to `ib` for most firms), and the conditioning SUMRANK of operating profitability plus cash cushion replicates the already-tested Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield family, so the marginal information content is minimal.

This is a rescaled recombination of two already-evaluated archive signals (Rising Interest Cost Profit Trap and Intangible Platform Glamour Fade), swapping the denominator to sales without introducing a new economic mechanism.
